page: The Vultr vc2-8c-32gb is an instance within the Cloud Compute family, positioned as a general-purpose virtual machine. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 2.0 GHz across 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory provision stands at 32.0 GB, providing an even 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). CPU cache layout includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Standard instruction set support includes AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, whereas modern extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are absent. Local storage is bundled as a 640 GB NVMe SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no dedicated GPUs attached.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate distinct performance disparities between single-core throughput and multi-threaded scaling on this shared architecture. Single-core tests fall into the lower tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 844.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 800.09 (both in the bottom 10%). Single-threaded compression is similarly constrained, measuring 15.6 GB/sec in gzip and 6.46 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-core operations perform nearer the median, reaching 6282.15 on stress-ng and 7986.55 on the PassMark CPU suite. Clang software compilation and ray tracing on Geekbench also land in the middle tier at 7232.0 and 5662.0 respectively.

Memory and I/O benchmarks reveal acceptable read speeds alongside bottlenecks under heavier uncached writes. Small block cached read throughput reaches 516.53 GB/sec, and large block uncached reads maintain 40.26 GB/sec, placing both in the middle 50%. However, large block uncached write bandwidth is limited to 14.02 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10% tier alongside an overall PassMark memory score of 1627.2. In-memory data storage demonstrates reasonable capability with Redis SET operations sustaining 7.55 million operations per second, though static web serving throughput drops to 5.79 GB/sec.

The instance delivers a cost-efficient hardware profile for workloads requiring generous allocations of RAM and fast local NVMe capacity without the premium associated with dedicated compute cores. However, the shared CPU topology, modest base clock rate, and constrained memory write performance make it suboptimal for write-intensive databases or single-threaded applications. The vc2-8c-32gb is best fitted for multi-threaded build environments, CI/CD runners, internal development staging, caching tiers, and standard web application hosting.
description: The Vultr vc2-8c-32gb is a general-purpose virtual instance belonging to the Cloud Compute family, providing 8 shared x86_64 Intel vCPUs (4 physical cores at 2.0 GHz), 32.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 640 GB NVMe SSD with zero GPUs. Delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is engineered for workloads requiring substantial capacity without dedicated core pricing. Benchmarks demonstrate restrained single-core performance, reflecting bottom-decile scores in Geekbench and stress-ng, alongside limited large-block uncached write bandwidth of 14.02 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks achieve median-tier results, reaching 7986.55 on PassMark CPU, 7.55 million Redis SET ops/sec, and solid Clang compilation throughput. The hardware profile offers reliable cost efficiency for multi-threaded background workers, CI/CD runners, staging nodes, and caching deployments that tolerate shared CPU resource contention.
